# Methodology

This document outlines the scientific methodology governing all experiments within the Neural Archaeology platform.

## 1. Causation over Correlation
Activation visualizations (e.g., showing what image activates a neuron most strongly) only prove *correlation*. To claim a neuron represents a feature, we must prove *causation* through Intervention (Ablation).
*   **Rule:** No scientific report generated by this system will claim a component "controls" a behavior without corresponding ablation data.

## 2. Experimental Controls
Every intervention must be compared against a statistically valid baseline.
*   **Ablation Control:** When ablating a target neuron to measure accuracy drop, the system must also automatically ablate a *randomly selected* neuron of the same layer to establish a baseline performance drop.
*   **Probe Control:** Linear probes trained on representations must be compared to probes trained on randomly initialized (untrained) representations.

## 3. Seed Stability
Findings that only appear in one random seed are considered artifacts, not fundamental properties of the architecture.
*   **Requirement:** Core architectural claims (e.g., "Layer 3 learns highly sparse representations") must be verified across a minimum of $N$ seeds (default $N=3$).

## 4. Hardware Independence
The scientific validity of an experiment must not depend on the compute environment. Floating-point variations across CPU/GPU boundaries must be documented, and random seeds must be fixed to ensure deterministic execution wherever mathematically possible.
